method: 34 approved members hold /api/events (timeout 25s) while one administrator broadcast is sent; 60 concurrent /api/agents requests run in a separate process from 3 ms before to after the broadcast. Server variants differ only in wakeEventWaiters: one synchronous pass over every waiter vs batches of 8 with setImmediate between batches.
dataset: fresh isolated data dir, one conversation, 34 members, Node 22.19.0, three runs per variant

senderIsolation.note: a separate process performed the POST; wall time includes ~45 ms Node process startup, so absolute values are not server latency

note: Every waiter received the broadcast in both variants. A write that lands during a batched pass sets wakeAgain and triggers another pass over the then-current waiters, so later messages are not missed; newly registered waiters cover the current state in their own first check().

autoforge.scope: adapter-reported build/test only; no runtime or deployment claim
limitations: operator-owned adapters run outside a sandbox
test_pass covers the targeted acceptance subset; the full node --test suite was run separately
autoforge.note: cumulative candidate contains the 2026-11-14 visibility, worker budget/paging and wake fan-out changes
